review.actual_role: Internal reference-keyed concurrent append-only micro-cache used for provider command initialization delegates.
review.hardest_behavior: Changing insertion or reset semantics requires tracing concurrent lookup, duplicate insertion, and clearing against immutable snapshots. Publication must preserve the chain, a competing insertion must be retried, and a caller losing a duplicate-key race must receive the already-published value through its ref parameter. These are interacting temporal invariants that are not established by a single sequential execution.
review.counterevidence: The concurrency surface is deliberately small: nodes are immutable, there is one head reference, no per-node removal, and matching is explicitly by object identity. The inspected caller tolerates independently constructing a candidate before insertion. These constraints make the proof substantially smaller than a general concurrent collection.
review.inspection_scope: Read SqlMapper.Link.cs completely (1-63). Searched Link usages in Dapper and inspected CommandDefinition.cs 125-205, including cache reset, lookup, delegate construction, and TryAdd. No execution or exhaustive concurrency-test review.

evidence.observation: The stated contract combines reference equality and thread safety with append-only values; Clear independently exchanges the shared head.
Lookup traverses an existing chain and uses identity equality; a successful lookup returns the stored value without mutating nodes.
TryAdd snapshots the head atomically, checks duplicates, returns a competing value by ref, and publishes only if the head still matches that snapshot; retry restarts the duplicate check.
Constructor-only Key, Value, and Tail initialization is part of the immutable-chain assumption on which concurrent traversal depends.

review.actual_role: Builds and compiles mapped-object CSV write delegates, coordinating mapping order, custom conversions, constants, converter options, null handling, and field output.
review.hardest_behavior: Changing generated field behavior requires distinguishing expression-construction time from later cached delegate execution while preserving mapping precedence and emitted field order. Custom conversion, constant conversion, ordinary member conversion, null records, and nested references take different paths; generated calls also affect the writer field type and output state. A meaningful change needs tracing these contracts across mapping, expression access, the cached writer, and output calls.
review.counterevidence: Member processing is sequential and assembled from separate delegates; mapping traversal, safe nested access, conversion, and actual CSV formatting are delegated to named helpers. Existing constant and null-writing tests provide concrete behavioral examples. There is no concurrency or asynchronous lifecycle in this class.
review.inspection_scope: Read ObjectRecordWriter.cs completely (1-121), RecordWriter.cs completely, Writing/ConstantTests.cs and Writing/WriteNullTests.cs completely. Inspected ExpressionManager.CreateGetMemberExpression (285-350), CsvWriter.WriteConvertedField (115-145), CsvWriter.CanWrite and record-type selection (685-730), and searched MemberMapCollection sorting/AddMembers locations. Did not execute tests or inspect every configuration combination.

evidence.observation: The generator may add an auto-map, flattens mapped members for ordering, and treats an empty map as an error before building any delegates.
A custom writing conversion constructs typed arguments and calls WriteField directly, then continues before the general CanWrite filter; changing order changes policy.
Constants use their runtime-type converter, while ordinary members require a configured converter and mutate merged options before embedding conversion calls in expressions.
Ordinary mapped access relies on ExpressionManager, wraps class records in a null conditional, and calls WriteConvertedField with the mapped field type. This differs from the custom-conversion path.
Per-member expression trees are compiled and combined into a later-executed action, so construction-time state and runtime writer effects must be considered separately.

review.actual_role: CSV enum converter supporting NameAttribute aliases, optional case-insensitive matching, ordinary enum parsing, and reverse alias formatting.
review.hardest_behavior: Changing alias acceptance or output selection requires tracing how three lookup tables are initialized and how their different collision rules interact with case sensitivity, duplicate underlying values, alias-first parsing, and ordinary enum fallback. Forward and reverse mappings are intentionally not a simple bijection; fallback failure and null formatting also inherit behavior from the base converter.
review.counterevidence: The dictionaries are populated only during construction and then read. Parsing ultimately delegates to framework enum operations; the focused enum test file supplies duplicate-name/value and case-sensitivity examples. There are no cross-record state transitions or broad orchestration responsibilities.
review.inspection_scope: Read EnumConverter.cs completely (1-116), TypeConversion/EnumConverterTests.cs completely, and DefaultTypeConverter.cs completely. Static review only; neither target-framework branch was executed.

evidence.observation: Exact aliases, case-insensitive aliases, and reverse value-to-name formatting are represented by separate dictionaries with different key semantics.

Initialization walks framework-enumerated values, resolves each name attribute, and preserves the first insertion separately in all three dictionaries; collisions and multiple aliases require tracing the resulting mappings.
The per-member ignore-case option selects the alias dictionary, and recognized aliases take precedence over framework parsing.
Two target-framework implementations use TryParse or Parse with catch, then delegate failures to the base converter.
Output uses the chosen reverse alias when present and otherwise uses base formatting, so accepted input aliases do not all become output spellings.

review.actual_role: Provider-independent DbException number matching through a cached, compiled accessor for a public integer Number property.
review.hardest_behavior: Changing supported exception shapes requires checking reflection validation, expression compilation, and the distinction between discovery-time failures returning no accessor and getter invocation failures propagating. Cache construction may occur more than once for a type under contention, but its stored helper is immutable and its purpose is localized.
review.counterevidence: The property contract is narrow and explicit: a readable public instance property of exactly the requested type. Missing or unsupported accessors produce false, and concurrency is delegated to ConcurrentDictionary. The helper has no caller-supplied mutation or elaborate invalidation lifecycle.
review.inspection_scope: Read DbExceptionExtensions.cs completely (1-64). Searched IsNumber tests and inspected ProviderTests.cs 65-125, which covers matching/nonmatching SQL-provider errors. No reflection edge-case execution or provider connection was attempted.

evidence.observation: The public extension handles a null exception; matching requires an accessor, whose invocation occurs outside the reflection/compilation catch.
A concurrent dictionary stores immutable per-type helpers, with check-then-create allowing duplicate helper construction rather than a complex coordinated initialization protocol.
Reflection restricts the Number contract to a readable public instance property of the exact type, compiles a cast/property-access lambda, and maps construction exceptions to a missing accessor.

review.actual_role: Documentation generator rendering a reflected type into Markdown with declaration, inheritance, constructors, fields, properties, and methods.
review.hardest_behavior: A declaration-rendering change needs a focused check of reflected type categories: suppress enum inheritance text, distinguish static from abstract classes without treating interfaces the same way, and preserve indexer parameter formatting. These are localized presentation assumptions rather than a stateful algorithm.
review.counterevidence: Most of the body independently emits a section if its prepared member collection is nonempty. Metadata gathering and ordering are performed by TypeInfo, and naming/summary formatting is delegated to helpers. There is no backtracking, transactional state, or interaction among the member sections beyond appending output.
review.inspection_scope: Read TypeGenerator.cs completely (1-118) and its TypeInfo.cs metadata builder completely (1-93). Did not execute the generator or inspect all naming-extension implementations.

evidence.observation: Declaration rendering locally combines enum inheritance suppression with mutually exclusive static/abstract modifiers based on reflection flags.
Inheritance, constructors, and fields are emitted as independent sections from prepared collections; these repeated presentation loops do not create coupled state.
Property rendering has one localized distinction for indexers, formatting their parameter types instead of the ordinary property name.
Method rendering directly appends names and summaries from the prepared method list, with no additional selection or lifecycle logic.

limitation: Exploratory strict-reversal selection; shared file in two pairs; one reviewer; no inferential test
